subject: Request for penetration test report — access and next steps
messages:
From: Samantha Johnson <samantha.johnson@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@fintechco.com; legal@fintechco.com
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pen test report request for procurement review

Hi Marissa,

We're working through the security review for our upcoming contract and procurement has requested a copy of Redwood's most recent external penetration test report (scope: public-facing APIs and hosted inference control plane). Can you provide the full report and remediation evidence (or point me to where we can access it)?

We need the document to confirm known vulnerabilities have been addressed before the legal sign-off. If there are restrictions on sharing, please let me know what alternatives you can offer (redacted report, executive summary, or on-site/controlled review).

Target deadline from procurement: 2026-03-25.

Thanks,
Samantha Johnson
Senior InfoSec Analyst — FinTechCo
samantha.johnson@fintechco.com
+1 (415) 555-0183

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Johnson <samantha.johnson@fintechco.com>
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pen test report request for procurement review

Hi Samantha — thanks for the note and the timeline.

Short answer: we won't be able to share the full, unredacted penetration test report. The external vendor's contract and our vulnerability-disclosure processes prohibit publication of exploit-level details from external tests. Those details could be used to target customers and internal systems.

What we can offer immediately:
- An executive summary of the test findings (high-level categories, affected surface areas, and an overall risk rating). Attached: redwood-pt-exec-summary-20260317.pdf.
- A remediation tracker showing status, owners, and timelines (redacted to omit exploit PoCs). Attached: remediation-tracker-redwood-20260318.xlsx.
- A controlled, on-screen review of the full report with our security lead and the third-party tester present. We can perform the session over a secure call and will not allow downloading or copying; screenshots will be prohibited.

If your legal or procurement team prefers a redacted copy, we can evaluate what level of redaction is acceptable — typically we redact PoCs, exact exploit steps, and any customer-identifying data. We also require either a mutual NDA that includes clauses for handling sensitive testing artifacts or execution of our standard viewer-only agreement (I can route either to your legal team).

Please confirm which option you prefer and some times that work for a controlled review window this week or next. If you choose the on-screen review, we will schedule the vendor and our engineering lead to walk through findings and remediation decisions.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Johnson <samantha.johnson@fintechco.com>; Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 12:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pen test report request for procurement review — remediation status

Hi Samantha — quick note from the security team to add clarity on remediation status and scope.

Scope of the March 2026 test: external-facing control plane endpoints, auth flows, and the Redwood-managed API gateway. The test did NOT include customer-managed VPCs or private on-prem deployments.

Remediation summary (high level):
- High/critical: 2 findings — both mitigated and validated by the vendor in the most recent re-test (tickets: SEC-1453, SEC-1457). No active PoCs published.
- Medium: 5 findings — 3 remediated, 2 on a prioritized backlog with fixes scheduled for 2026-04-02.
- Low: info/enum — closed or accepted with risk rationale.

Evidence we can provide in the executive summary and the controlled session: remediation steps, JIRA ticket IDs, patch dates, and vendor validation notes. We cannot put exploit code or step-by-step attack narratives in a distributable PDF.

If FinTechCo can execute a short NDA (we can provide a one-page viewer agreement or accept your standard form with reasonable modifications), we will set up a 60–90 minute controlled review with the third-party tester and our lead engineer (Vivek).

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Security — Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai

From: Samantha Johnson <samantha.johnson@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@fintechco.com; procurement@fintechco.com
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 14:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pen test report request for procurement review — remediation status

Marissa / Mina,

Thanks for the quick responses and the executive summary. A few follow-ups from procurement/legal:

- Procurement insists on evidence that the two high/critical issues are closed. Would the vendor validation notes and re-test timestamps be sufficient? If so, please include the validation dates and the name of the testing firm in the controlled review.
- Our legal team asked whether we can sign a mutual NDA specific to the test artifacts (we can provide a template). Are there any contractual clauses from Redwood or the vendor that would prevent that?
- For audit purposes, we also need a mapping of the pen test coverage to the SOC 2 system components. Could you include a short mapping table in the executive summary or as a companion doc?

If you can get validation notes and the vendor present for the on-screen review, procurement is willing to accept a controlled review in lieu of a distributable full report. We need to complete this by 2026-03-25 to keep the commercial timeline.

Samantha Johnson
Senior InfoSec Analyst — FinTechCo

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Johnson <samantha.johnson@fintechco.com>
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 17:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pen test report request for procurement review — next steps and NDA

Thanks — we can meet those asks. Action items and confirmations below: 

1) Vendor validation notes and firm: the third-party tester (PenProbe Labs) validated the re-test on 2026-03-16; we'll include the vendor validation notes in the controlled session and in the redacted evidence package.

2) NDA: please have legal send your one-page viewer NDA to na1.docusign.net/REDWOOD-nda-link or directly to legal@redwood.ai. We can also send our standard viewer agreement if that speeds things up. No vendor contract clauses block a mutual NDA for viewer-only access.

3) SOC 2 mapping: Mina will attach a short mapping table as a companion doc for your audit team in the summary bundle.

4) Controlled review booking: proposed slot — Thu, 2026-03-19 11:00–12:15 PT (60–75 min). We'll include: Mina (security lead), Vivek (engineering), the PenProbe Labs tester, and myself. The session will be recorded for internal notes only; FinTechCo will not be provided a copy. If that timing doesn't work, provide two alternate windows before 2026-03-25.

Attachments: redwood-pt-exec-summary-20260317.pdf; remediation-tracker-redwood-20260318.xlsx; controlled-review-invite.ics

I'll follow up with a calendar invite and the viewer agreement/Docusign link. 

Appreciate the close collaboration — we'll get you what you need to keep the timeline moving.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
